story.iWant: a service that wraps Keycloak user operations
story.soThat: MCP and CLI can share the same logic
story.tasks:
- [ ] **T1 – Implement `UserService` core operations** - [ ] Define `User`, `CreateUserInput`, `UpdateUserInput`, and any list/pagination types in `src/lib/keycloak/types.ts` consistent with `docs/architecture.md`. - [ ] Implement `UserService` in `src/lib/keycloak/services/users.ts` with the method surface defined in the acceptance criteria, delegating to `client.users.*`. - [ ] Ensure `UserService` obtains its `KcAdminClient` instance via the shared `getKeycloakClient()` helper and never instantiates the client directly. - [ ] Wrap connectivity/auth failures and logical errors in `IdentiKeyError` with appropriate `ErrorCodes` (`USER_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_INPUT`, `CONNECTION_FAILED`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, etc.).
- [ ] **T2 – Implement user mappers and exports** - [ ] Add `mapKeycloakUser` (and any helpers) under `src/lib/keycloak/mappers/users.ts` to map Keycloak `UserRepresentation` into the IdentiKey `User` type, including `guilds` from group memberships. - [ ] Expose `UserService` (and its factory, if any) from `src/lib/keycloak/services/index.ts` so MCP and CLI can share it. - [ ] Ensure naming and file layout match the service-first patterns in `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/epics.md` (services per domain, no Keycloak types leaking through).
- [ ] **T3 – Tests and diagnostics** - [ ] Add Vitest coverage for `UserService.list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `resetPassword`, `getCredentials`, and `deleteCredential` using mocks of `@keycloak/keycloak-admin-client`. - [ ] Verify error paths produce `IdentiKeyError` with stable codes and scrubbed messages, not raw Keycloak errors. - [ ] Add at least one higher-level test that exercises `UserService` via the same config/client wiring used by CLI/MCP, to catch regressions in how the service is constructed.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **UserService surface** - Given an authenticated Keycloak client When `UserService` is instantiated Then the following methods are available:
| Method | FR | Description | | ----------------------------------------- | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | `list(options?)` | FR5 | List users with pagination (max, offset) | | `search(query, options?)` | FR6 | Search by username, email, firstName, lastName | | `get(id)` | FR7 | Get user by ID | | `create(data)` | FR8 | Create user with username, email, firstName, lastName, enabled | | `update(id, data)` | FR9 | Update user attributes | | `delete(id)` | FR10 | Delete user | | `resetPassword(id, password, temporary?)` | FR11 | Set new password | | `getCredentials(id)` | FR12 | List user credentials | | `deleteCredential(id, credentialId)` | FR13 | Remove specific credential |
2. **Domain modeling** - All methods return IdentiKey domain types (not raw Keycloak types).
3. **Error handling** - All failures are wrapped in `IdentiKeyError` using appropriate `ErrorCodes` rather than exposing raw Keycloak errors.

doc.title: keycloak-commander — Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: User Management FRs: - FR5: Admins can list all users with pagination - FR6: Admins can search users by username, email, first name, or last name - FR7: Admins can get detailed information for a specific user - FR8: Admins can create new users with required attributes - FR9: Admins can update user attributes (name, email, enabled status, etc.) - FR10: Admins can delete users - FR11: Admins can reset a user's password - FR12: Admins can view a user's credentials (passkeys, OTP devices, etc.) - FR13: Admins can delete specific credentials from a user

doc.title: keycloak-commander — Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet:
As an **admin**, I want **a service that wraps Keycloak user operations**, So that **MCP and CLI can share the same logic**.
UserService methods: - list, search, get, create, update, delete, resetPassword, getCredentials, deleteCredential All methods return IdentiKey domain types and wrap errors in IdentiKeyError.

doc.title: Architecture — keycloak-commander
Epic Technical Specification: Epic 1 – Foundation
doc.snippet:
Epic 1 defines the shared contracts that UserService must rely on: - Configuration: loadConfig() from config.ts with validated KEYCLOAK_* env vars. - Client: getKeycloakClient() from client.ts providing a singleton authenticated KcAdminClient. - Errors: IdentiKeyError and ErrorCodes for connectivity and domain failures. - Logging: Pino-based logger instance, with connection validation via validateConnection().
UserService should consume these contracts instead of re-implementing configuration or connectivity logic.

artifact.reason: Defines the IdentiKey user domain model and input types that UserService will expose to MCP and CLI.
Maps Keycloak UserRepresentation into the IdentiKey User type, including guild memberships derived from groups.
Implements the core user operations on top of KcAdminClient, using getKeycloakClient(), IdentiKeyError, and domain mappers.
Provides a shared factory or export for UserService that MCP and CLI can consume without duplicating wiring logic.
Provides the standardized error type and codes used when user operations fail (e.g., USER_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_INPUT, CONNECTION_FAILED, UNAUTHORIZED).
Structured logger used by UserService for diagnostics without leaking credentials or secrets.
Vitest coverage for UserService methods and error mapping using a mocked Keycloak admin client.

story-context.constraints: - UserService must depend on the shared connectivity, configuration, error, and logging primitives from Epic 1 (loadConfig, getKeycloakClient, IdentiKeyError, ErrorCodes, logger, validateConnection) instead of re-implementing them. - All public methods of UserService must return IdentiKey domain types and must not expose raw Keycloak representations or internal IDs that don't map cleanly to the IdentiKey model. - Error handling for user operations must use IdentiKeyError with specific error codes (e.g., USER_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_INPUT, CONNECTION_FAILED, UNAUTHORIZED); generic or ad-hoc error strings are not allowed. - Logging in UserService should be minimal but structured, using the shared logger and never including passwords, tokens, secrets, or full credential objects in log payloads.
story-context.interfaces:
- UserService API: - `constructor(client: KcAdminClient)` - `async list(options?: ListOptions): Promise<User[]>` - `async search(query: string, options?: ListOptions): Promise<User[]>` - `async get(id: string): Promise<User>` - `async create(data: CreateUserInput): Promise<User>` - `async update(id: string, data: UpdateUserInput): Promise<User>` - `async delete(id: string): Promise<void>` - `async resetPassword(id: string, password: string, temporary?: boolean): Promise<void>` - `async getCredentials(id: string): Promise<unknown[]>` - `async deleteCredential(id: string, credentialId: string): Promise<void>`
- Service factory: - `async getUserService(): Promise<UserService>` — obtains an authenticated client via getKeycloakClient() and returns a UserService instance.

tests.standards: Use Vitest unit tests with a mocked @keycloak/keycloak-admin-client to verify that UserService methods call the correct Keycloak APIs, map results into IdentiKey domain types, and wrap errors in IdentiKeyError with appropriate codes. Avoid real network calls in CI; reserve any real-instance tests for manual smoke testing once a dev realm is available.
tests.ideas: - Verify that list/search use Keycloak's users.find with search, first, and max parameters and map results into User[] with guilds resolved from groups. - Simulate a missing user in get(id) and assert that UserService throws an IdentiKeyError with code USER_NOT_FOUND. - Simulate invalid input to create/update and assert that UserService surfaces INVALID_INPUT rather than raw Keycloak validation errors. - Simulate connectivity/auth failures and ensure they are propagated as IdentiKeyError with CONNECTION_FAILED or UNAUTHORIZED and that no secrets appear in any logged payloads.
